The worst restaurant experience in 2023-2024.
Aug 2024 • Solo
Went to the restaurant today to try Adjarian Khachapuri since I'm Georgian missing the authentic taste of Georgian cuisine, and they do have that. 
The atmosphere in the restaurant was nice, however, when I went through 
the menu, I noticed that traditional dishes from different countries of the region such as Ukraine, Georgia, Russia, and Armenia were mixed up
together under the label of the restaurant called "Ararat" which is the province and the town in Armenia. 
They had Khinkali on the menu, described as a "Georgian Dumpling" (Indicating that It has something to do with the Chinese or Asian culture) and is served in pieces (khinkali is usually served in at least 5 pieces together).
Then, they had an Armenian version of Khashlama, without clearly indicating whether it was Armenian or Georgian. It is really easy to 
confuse the dishes and get the impression that certain dishes 
originated from Armenia because the restaurant is located in a place, where people mainly are unfamiliar with the Caucasus/ Eastern Europe
The restaurant has a responsibility to represent the countries and the dishes.
As for the Adjarian Khachapuri, that's exactly how I would make
 it if I wanted someone to lose interest in the country and its cuisine forever. (which by the way, is one of the best in the world!) 
Leaving Alone the PM problem, when I tried to address this issue with the manager/owner, instead of treating me as a customer and directly addressing the issue, I ended up talking to someone, who had no listening culture and interrupted me each time I tried to deliver the idea,
was constantly in the defensive mode, paraphrasing my words, pushing irrelevant narratives, (she mentioned that she was proficient in English?!), and Inclining that my feedback was coming from an emotional state (It was not); somehow admitting that the menu has to be updated but still telling me how she wouldn't just sit a listen to my opinion about HER business when I pointed out that she was not allowing me to speak or finish any sentence. Now this review does come from the emotional state. of a great disappointment.

Just don't go there.

Authentic Armenian cuisine in a very cozy home-like atmosphere
Apr 2022
Have been living and exploring dining options in Thao Dien for over one year. Ararat is definitely on the top of my list. The restaurant is run by an Armenian family - good people passionate about their business. After a few visits, you somehow start feeling close to them and the place feels more and more like home. They offer really good quality Armenian food, BBQ, and homemade wines in a cozy stylish atmosphere. My favorite dishes are lamb kebab, khachapuri adjarian and okroshka (cold soup) . The place is great for dinner and after-dinner relaxation with drinks and shisha. 

Since at the moment all tables are in the outdoor courtyard, the place is super-comfortable at night, but a bit too hot during the daytime. Therefore, not the best option for lunch.
